_weather: 「洞口透进灰白的天光，雨停了」 — the rain is over, a grey dawn

setup.zh: 天亮了，狐狸不见了。洞口坐着一个银发赤脚的姑娘，金色的竖瞳，正在吃你留作早饭的那个饼角。
setup.en: Day has come and the fox is gone. At the cave mouth sits a barefoot girl with silver hair and gold slit eyes, eating the corner of flatbread you saved for breakfast.

recap.zh: 天亮时，那只狐狸成了一个银发的姑娘：青丘之主，只记得自己叫银月；她看见吴婆婆的木牌，变了脸色。
recap.en: At daybreak the fox was a silver-haired girl: mistress of Qingqiu, remembering only that her name was Yinyue; the sight of Granny Wu's token changed her face.

zh: 银发垂到腰下，赤着脚，衣白如雪。
身后一条银尾，只有一条。
en: Someone sits at the cave mouth.
Silver hair to her waist, bare feet, a robe white as snow.
One silver tail behind her. Only one.

story.zh:
小满是给一阵吧唧嘴的声音吵醒的。火堆已经熄了，洞口透进灰白的天光，雨停了。他怀里空空的，那件外衣叠得整整齐齐放在一边，狐狸却不见了。

洞口坐着一个人，是个姑娘，看着比他大不了几岁，一头银发直垂到腰下，赤着脚，身上裹着一件他从没见过的衣裳，白得像雪，又亮得像水。她背对着他，正在吃东西，吃的是他藏在包袱最底下、准备当早饭的那个饼角。

她一面嚼，一面道：「难吃。」说着又咬了一大口。

小满望着那个饼角，心里一阵绞痛：曾经有一个饼角放在他包袱的最底下，他没有吃，留着当早饭；等到给人吃了，才后悔莫及。人世间最痛苦的事，莫过于此。他悄悄地把手摸向身边一块石头。

她头也不回，道：「放下。」跟着朗声道：「本王乃青丘之主，仙界妖王。统御万妖，号令八荒，一怒则山崩，一笑则花开——」小满插口道：「那你为什么吃我的饼？」她道：「——饿了。」

山洞里静了三息。一只乌鸦从洞口飞过，「嘎、嘎」叫了两声，听来很像在笑。

她转过头来，金色的眼睛，瞳仁竖着，瞥了一眼他手里的石头，嘴角一翘，道：「不错。知道先摸石头，不是先喊娘。」

说着站起身，走到他面前，上上下下地打量他，便如在集市上挑一棵不太新鲜的白菜，道：「十二岁。筋骨嘛，还算凑合。眼神，也还凑合。灵根——」她咂了一下嘴，「本王一眼就瞧得出来，这辈子修不成仙的那种。啧。烂成这样。」

小满道：「……你是那只狐狸？」她喝道：「放肆！本王的名讳，乃是——」说到这里，忽然顿住了，眉头越皱越紧，「乃是……」小满便等着。一只松鼠从洞口探进头来，看了看他们，也等着。

她道：「……你先说你叫什么。」小满道：「你忘了？」她脸上一下子涨得通红，道：「本王没忘！本王是——」咳了一声，「考考你！」小满道：「沈小满。」她道：「好。答对了。」小满道：「……你还没说你叫什么。」她道：「本王……」

那松鼠等不下去，走了。她憋了半天，憋得脸都红了，终于憋出两个字来：「……[银月]{注=yinyue}。」跟着又道：「对。银月。本王，就叫银月。」

她长长地松了一口气，随即又理直气壮起来，下巴一抬，道：「凡人！你救了本王，本王许你一个心愿。说吧，要什么？长生不老？富甲天下？娶一个仙女？」

小满想了想，认认真真地想了很久，道：「……把饼还我。」

她张着嘴，那句「娶一个仙女」还挂在嘴边没收回去，一双金眼睛瞪得溜圆。半晌，她低头看了看手里只剩一个小角的饼，又抬头看了看他，然后非常、非常郑重地，双手捧着那个饼角，便如捧着一方传国玉玺——放进了自己嘴里，嚼了两嚼，咽了下去，道：「一言为定。本王，欠你一张饼。」

小满张着嘴瞧着她。晨光里，她身后那一条银白的尾巴轻轻摆了摆，只有一条，尾根上八道整整齐齐的断口，在光底下看得清清楚楚。他忽然就不想要饼了，问道：「……你疼吗？」

她愣住了，看着他，看了很久，久到树上的露珠落下来三颗，每一颗都「叮」地响了一声。那双冷得像井水的金色眼睛里，有什么东西晃了一下。然后她把脸扭开了，道：「……本王是妖王。妖王，不知道什么叫疼。」

这句话，她说得极快，快得像是怕说慢了，便要说成别的什么。

她低下头来，便在这时，瞧见了他搁在地下的那块木牌，眼睛一下子睁大了，声音也变了：「这个。哪来的？」小满道：「村里吴婆婆给的。她说……我爷爷当年进山，也从她门口过。」

银月盯着那块木牌，盯了很久，然后把它捡起来还给了他，什么也没说。一个妖王欠他的东西，连凭据都叫她吃进了肚里。

她拍了拍衣裳上根本不存在的灰，又恢复了那副妖王的模样，把下巴一抬，道：「这山谷，本王待够了。」说着两只光脚在地下轻轻一跺，只见她脚底下腾起一团白蒙蒙的云气，托着她，悠悠地升了起来，一尺，两尺，三尺……小满仰着脖子看，嘴张得能塞进一个鸡蛋。

升到半丈来高，那团云忽然晃了一晃，像一锅揭了盖的水汽，「噗」的一声，散了。她「啊哟」一声，手脚在半空里乱划了两下，像一只给人扔下水的猫，直掉下来，「扑通」一屁股坐在了草地上，两只光脚丫子朝了天。那草一圈一圈地亮开去，亮得很是好看，倒像满谷的草都在瞧她的笑话。

方才等不下去走了的那只松鼠，不知什么时候又回来了，蹲在洞口一块石头上，瞧得十分认真。

小满赶紧低下头去，看自己的脚趾头，腮帮子咬得死紧，憋得眼泪都出来了。

她坐在地下，也不起来，脸涨得通红，连两只耳朵尖都红透了，道：「……不许笑。」小满道：「我没笑。」她道：「你肩膀在抖。」小满道：「我那是冷的。」她瞪了他半天，这才慢吞吞地站起身来，一本正经地道：「本王是在试一试，这地的软硬。」小满道：「软吗？」她道：「……还行。」顿了一顿，又低声嘟囔起来，倒像私塾里的孩子背书，背给自己听的：「人之生，气之聚也；聚则为生，散则为死。」背完了，她揪下一根草，拿两个鼻孔对着他，道：「本王是饿散的。」又道：「……你爹的膝盖撂挑子，你也没笑话他。」小满一愣。

他爹的膝盖撂挑子，是他昨儿夜里，跟一只闭着眼睛的狐狸说的。他又想起昨儿夜里跟它说过的旁的话：桂花糕，疼了不说的规矩，还有他那一嗓子「这几笔账，我找谁要去」——脸上不由得一阵发烫，也不知道这些话，它到底听去了多少。

她却已把脸扭开了，四下里望了一望。这山谷四面都是崖，崖上垂着藤，银叶树一棵挨着一棵，棵棵长得一模一样。小满便问：「你认得路吗？」

她道：「本王是妖王。」小满道：「妖王认得路吗？」她道：「妖王是飞的。」小满道：「飞的认得路吗？」她不答了。小满心想，这笔账倒也不难算：她会飞，可眼下飞不起来；自己不会飞，可一路走进来，崖壁上一段划了一道，道道都在。

一个飞不起来的妖王，和一个会在崖壁上划道道的猎户家孩子，眼下是后一个值钱些。她大约也算明白了，咳了一声，道：「走吧，凡人。先带本王出去。」
story.en:
Xiaoman was woken by the sound of someone smacking their lips. The fire was out; grey daylight came in at the mouth of the cave; the rain had stopped. His arms were empty. The jacket lay folded neatly to one side, and the fox was gone.

Someone was sitting at the mouth of the cave: a girl, who looked only a few years older than him, with silver hair falling straight past her waist, bare feet, and wrapped in clothes such as he'd never seen, white as snow and bright as water. She had her back to him and was eating something — the corner of flatbread he'd hidden at the very bottom of his bundle for breakfast.

As she chewed she said, "Disgusting." And took another big bite.

Xiaoman looked at that corner of flatbread and felt a twist of pain in his heart. Once there was a corner of flatbread at the bottom of his bundle; he did not eat it, he saved it for breakfast; only when somebody else had eaten it did he regret it, too late. Of all the sorrows of this world, none is greater than this. Quietly he slid his hand towards a stone beside him.

Without looking round she said, "Put it down." Then, in a ringing voice: "This queen is Lady of Qingqiu, Demon Queen of the immortal realm. Ten thousand demons answer to me; the eight wildernesses obey my word. When I rage, mountains fall; when I smile, flowers bloom—" Xiaoman cut in: "Then why are you eating my flatbread?" She said, "—I was hungry."

For three breaths the cave was silent. A crow flew past the mouth of the cave going *caw, caw*, and it sounded very much like laughing.

She turned her head. Golden eyes, slit pupils. She glanced at the stone in his hand and the corner of her mouth went up. "Not bad. Knows to grab a stone first instead of calling for his mother."

She stood up, came over, and looked him up and down like someone at the market picking over a cabbage that isn't very fresh. "Twelve years old. Bones and sinews — so-so. The eyes — also so-so. Spirit root—" she clicked her tongue, "this queen can tell at a glance: the kind that will never become an immortal in this life. Tsk. Rotten through."

Xiaoman said, "…Are you that fox?" She snapped, "How dare you! This queen's name is—" And there she stopped short. Her brows drew tighter and tighter. "Is…" Xiaoman waited. A squirrel poked its head in at the mouth of the cave, looked at them, and waited too.

She said, "…You say your name first." Xiaoman said, "You've forgotten?" Her face flushed bright red at once. "This queen has not forgotten! This queen is—" She coughed. "Testing you!" Xiaoman said, "Shen Xiaoman." She said, "Good. Correct." Xiaoman said, "…You still haven't said your name." She said, "This queen…"

The squirrel couldn't wait any longer, and left. She strained for a long time, strained till her face was red, and finally squeezed out two syllables: "…[Yinyue]{注=yinyue}." Then: "Yes. Yinyue. This queen is called Yinyue."

She let out a long breath of relief, and at once she was all righteous confidence again. Up went her chin. "Mortal! You saved this queen. This queen grants you one wish. Speak. What will it be? Eternal life? Riches beyond counting? A fairy for a wife?"

Xiaoman thought about it. He thought about it very seriously, for a long time, and said, "…Give me back my flatbread."

Her mouth hung open, "a fairy for a wife" still dangling on her lips unretracted, her golden eyes round as coins. After a long moment she looked down at the flatbread in her hand, of which only a small corner remained, then looked up at him, and then, very, very solemnly, holding the corner in both hands as if it were the imperial seal of the realm — put it into her own mouth, chewed twice, swallowed, and said: "Agreed. This queen owes you one flatbread."

Xiaoman gaped at her. In the morning light the silver-white tail behind her swished gently. Just the one, and at its root eight stumps, cut clean and even, perfectly clear in the light. All at once he didn't want the flatbread any more. He asked, "…Does it hurt?"

She froze and looked at him, looked at him for a long time — so long that three drops of dew fell from the trees, and each one went *ting*. In those golden eyes, cold as well water, something wavered. Then she turned her face away. "…This queen is a demon queen. A demon queen doesn't know what hurting is."

She said it very fast, so fast it was as if she was afraid that if she said it slowly, it would come out as something else.

She lowered her head, and at that moment saw the wooden tablet he'd put down on the ground. Her eyes went wide all at once, and her voice changed: "This. Where did you get it?" Xiaoman said, "Granny Wu in our village gave it to me. She said… when my grandpa went into the mountains, he passed her door too."

Yinyue stared at the tablet, stared for a long time. Then she picked it up, handed it back to him, and said nothing. What a demon queen owed him — and she'd eaten the receipt.

She brushed some dust that wasn't there off her clothes and was back to being a demon queen again. Up went her chin. "This queen has had enough of this valley." She stamped her two bare feet lightly on the ground, and a puff of milky cloud rose up under her and bore her up, floating gently, one foot, two feet, three feet… Xiaoman craned his neck to watch, his mouth open wide enough to fit an egg.

At about five feet up the cloud suddenly wobbled, like the steam off a pot with the lid lifted, and with a *pff* it was gone. She went "Ah!", flailed her arms and legs in mid-air like a cat thrown in the water, dropped straight down, and landed with a *thump* on her bottom in the grass, both bare feet in the air. The grass lit up ring after ring around her, very prettily, as if the whole valley's grass were laughing at her.

The squirrel that had got tired of waiting and left had come back at some point, and sat on a stone at the mouth of the cave, watching very closely.

Xiaoman quickly looked down at his toes, clenching his jaw so hard his eyes watered.

She sat on the ground without getting up, her face flaming, even the tips of her ears gone red. "…No laughing." Xiaoman said, "I'm not laughing." She said, "Your shoulders are shaking." Xiaoman said, "That's because I'm cold." She glared at him for a long time before slowly getting to her feet, and said, very properly, "This queen was testing how hard the ground is." Xiaoman said, "Is it soft?" She said, "…Not bad." After a pause she began muttering again, under her breath, like a child at school reciting a lesson to herself: "A man's life is the gathering of qi; gathered, it is life; scattered, it is death." When she'd finished reciting she yanked up a blade of grass and, pointing both nostrils at him, said, "This queen scattered from hunger." Then: "…When your father's knee walked off the job, you didn't laugh at him either." Xiaoman stopped.

His father's knee walking off the job was something he'd said last night, to a fox with its eyes shut. He thought of the other things he'd said to it last night: osmanthus cake, the rule about not saying it hurts, and that shout of "who am I supposed to collect those debts from" — and his face went hot. He had no idea how much of it the fox had actually heard.

But she'd already turned her face away and was looking around. The valley was cliffs on every side, vines hanging down them, silver-leafed trees one after another, every one of them exactly the same. So Xiaoman asked, "Do you know the way?"

She said, "This queen is a demon queen." Xiaoman said, "Do demon queens know the way?" She said, "Demon queens fly." Xiaoman said, "Do flying ones know the way?" She didn't answer. Xiaoman thought this sum wasn't hard either: she could fly, but right now she couldn't get off the ground; he couldn't fly, but all the way in he'd scratched a line on the cliff every so often, and every one was still there.

A demon queen who couldn't get off the ground and a hunter's boy who scratched lines on cliffs: right now the second was worth more. She seemed to have worked it out too. She coughed. "Come along, mortal. You may lead this queen out first."

label.en: Take her out of the valley

exits.means: goes with her, leaves the valley, heads back toward father

story.zh:
她侧过耳朵，朝崖顶那边听了一听，又道：「你爹就在你拽他的那道坡上，喊了你一夜。这会儿不喊了。」小满心里一松，跟着又一紧：「……不喊了？」

「他在解腰带，」她道，「解了腰带，又解绑腿，一截一截地接，一头拴在坡上的树根上。」她瞥了他一眼，「再不去，他要顺着崖往下爬了。」
story.en:
She turned an ear towards the top of the cliff, listened a moment, and said, "Your father is on that slope where you hauled him in. He called for you all night. He's stopped calling now." Xiaoman's heart eased, then tightened again. "…Stopped calling?"

"He's undoing his belt," she said. "Undone his belt, now his leg wrappings, tying them together piece by piece, one end lashed to a tree root on the slope." She cast him a glance. "If you don't go now, he's going to climb down the cliff."

refuse.zh: 银叶树棵棵一样——认着崖壁上你划的道道走。
refuse.en: Every silver tree looks the same — follow the lines you scratched on the cliff.

_beats: 认路 (yinyue-way, batch two 2026-10-14): played at the end of the passage, on 「先带本王出去」 — the valley a small fogged grid, the grass glowing where he walks, his marks on the cells by the cliff; follow them from the cave back to the moss where he fell (she points the way after 30 steps); grade straight · wandered → `way-straight` · `way-wandered`; 带她出谷 waits for it
